methods.label: Count face pairs with opposite parity
methods.explanation:
A sum is odd exactly when one die shows an odd number and the other shows an even number.

The die with \(4\) replaced by \(3\) has faces \(1,2,3,3,5,6\), so it has four odd faces and two even faces. The other die has faces \(1,2,4,4,5,6\), so it has two odd faces and four even faces. Repeated labels still belong to separate, equally likely faces.

The independent rolls give \(6\cdot6=36\) equally likely ordered face pairs. There are \(4\cdot4=16\) pairs with the first die odd and the second even, and \(2\cdot2=4\) pairs with the first even and the second odd. These cases cannot overlap and include every odd sum. Therefore the probability is
\[
\frac{16+4}{36}=\boxed{\frac59},
\]
choice \(\mathrm D\).
